name: mdxstudio-vscode
//private: Deliberately not private. vsce refuses to publish a private package, and this one is published - to the VS Code marketplace, not to npm. There is no `npm publish --workspaces` anywhere in this repository; every package is published by name, so nothing here will push this to the npm registry by accident.
description: Preview .mdx files in VS Code with the mdxstudio renderer: callouts, tabs, charts, flow graphs and Mermaid diagrams, themed to match the editor.
author: Suraj Donthi
//type: Deliberately CommonJS. The extension host loads `main` with require(); only the build script is ESM, and it says so with its .mjs extension.
//capabilities: The preview evaluates the document's own `{...}` expressions with `new Function`, which is why the webview's CSP normally grants 'unsafe-eval'. In an untrusted workspace that would mean a freshly cloned repository executing its own JavaScript in the editor as soon as an .mdx file is clicked, so the extension pins itself to the non-evaluating literal walker and drops 'unsafe-eval' from the policy until trust is granted. `mdxstudio.config` is the same decision with nothing to fall back to - loading a workspace's mdxstudio.config.js runs a module of that workspace's own code - so an untrusted workspace loads none at all. Everything else - rendering, scroll sync, the outline - works untrusted.

untrustedWorkspaces.description: The preview renders, but MDX `{...}` expressions are only read literally and the workspace's mdxstudio.config.js is not loaded: both would let an untrusted repository run its own code in the editor. Grant trust to enable them.

contributes.//commands: The product name is in the `title` rather than in a `category` on purpose. The title bar button's tooltip shows the title alone, and for a .md file this button sits next to VS Code's own markdown preview button - 'Open Preview to the Side' on both would be indistinguishable. Spelling it out keeps the palette entries namespaced under 'MDX Studio' at the same time.

commands.title: MDX Studio: Open Preview to the Side

contributes.//menus: `$(book)` because both preview codicons are already taken on a .md file: markdown-language-features gives `markdown.showPreviewToSide` `$(open-preview)` and `markdown.reopenAsPreview` `$(preview)`, and all three land in the same navigation group. A book reads as -render this document- and is unmistakable next to them. Markdown gets the button - use this renderer when you want its components and diagrams - but never the auto-open.

commandPalette.when: resourceLangId == mdx || resourceExtname == .mdx || resourceLangId == markdown || mdxstudio.previewFocus
resourceLangId == mdx || resourceExtname == .mdx || resourceLangId == markdown || mdxstudio.previewFocus

contributes.//keybindings: The Markdown preview's own chords, scoped to .mdx so they never clash: on a .md file `ctrl+shift+v` and `ctrl+k v` still belong to the built-in preview. Markdown reaches this renderer through the title bar button and the palette instead.

keybindings.//: Scoped to the focused preview so the editor's own font-size zoom keeps these chords everywhere else.

enumDescriptions: Evaluate `{...}` expressions with real JavaScript semantics. The preview's content security policy has to allow 'unsafe-eval' for this, because the renderer compiles each expression with `new Function`.

Only build values the syntax spells out - strings, numbers, booleans, arrays, plain objects. Needs no eval, so the preview runs under a CSP without 'unsafe-eval'. Component props still work; expressions in the document body do not.
mdxstudio.expressions.markdownDescription: How much of an MDX `{...}` expression the preview evaluates. Changing this reloads open previews. In a workspace you have not trusted this is forced to `literals` whatever it says, because `full` needs `'unsafe-eval'`.

enumDescriptions: Re-render while you type, after `mdxstudio.preview.delay` milliseconds of quiet.
Re-render only when the document is saved.
Re-render only when you run `MDX Studio: Refresh Preview`.
mdxstudio.updateMode.markdownDescription: When the preview re-renders. `onSave` and `manual` are for very large documents, where a diagram-heavy render on every keystroke is more than the machine wants to do.

mdxstudio.autoPreview.markdownDescription: Open the preview beside the editor whenever an `.mdx` file is opened, without moving focus out of the editor. One preview is reused for every document rather than one panel per file. Closing the preview stops it reopening for that file; opening a different `.mdx` file brings it back. Turn this off to open previews only from the command or the editor title bar.

mdxstudio.preview.delay.markdownDescription: Milliseconds to wait after the last keystroke before re-rendering the preview. Only applies when `#mdxstudio.updateMode#` is `onType`.

mdxstudio.highlightCurrentLine.description: Mark the block the editor's cursor is in with a rule down its left edge.

mdxstudio.customCss.markdownDescription: A `.css` file loaded into the preview after the shipped stylesheet, so it can override the `--mdxstudio-*` variables. Workspace-relative (`.vscode/preview.css`) or absolute. The preview reloads when the file changes on disk.

mdxstudio.config.markdownDescription: Where the preview looks for `mdxstudio.config.js` — the file that registers your own components with the renderer, the same file `npx @mdxstudio/cli` reads. Empty (the default) looks for `mdxstudio.config.js` then `mdxstudio.config.mjs` in the workspace folder the document belongs to; a path (workspace-relative or absolute) names one file; `off` never loads one. **Loading a config runs that project's JavaScript in the preview, so it is never loaded in a workspace you have not trusted, whatever this says.** The preview reloads when the file changes on disk.

mdxstudio.preview.showFrontmatterHeader.description: Render the document's YAML frontmatter as a header card at the top of the preview.

mdxstudio.preview.collapsibleHeadings.description: Let a reader fold the section under an H1, H2 or H3. The control that copies a heading's link is unaffected, and the PDF export always has every section open.

mdxstudio.preview.scrollPreviewWithEdito.description: Scroll the preview to match the editor's position. Sync points are the document's headings.

mdxstudio.preview.scrollEditorWithPrevie.description: Scroll the editor to match the preview's position. Sync points are the document's headings.

//dependencies: Declared so npm links the workspace packages and pins the React the preview bundle is built against. `build.mjs` resolves the @mdxstudio/* specifiers to `packages/*/src` rather than to their built `dist`, exactly as apps/studio's Vite config does, so the extension never needs `npm run build:packages` first.
